pluginRevision: kookr-toolkit-poc@0.0.1 (synthetic POC fixture: one sentinel skill + benign hook)

gates.evidence: Two independent hook sources (simulated user + Kookr monitoring) both executed for every lifecycle event in the same session; merging across ~/.grok/hooks, ~/.claude/settings.json and plugin hooks is documented and observed.
A harmless `echo` tool call fired pre_tool_use and post_tool_use with toolName=run_terminal_command and toolInput.command; the command executed (exit 0). Stable sessionId correlates the events.

A blocking permission produces a reliable structured signal: a Kookr PreToolUse hook receives toolName+toolInput and returns an explicit deny decision; the blocked command never runs (no post_tool_use). CAVEAT: the advertised dedicated PermissionDenied event did NOT fire for --deny-rule or hook-deny blocks in headless -p; Kookr must detect blocks via PreToolUse-without-PostToolUse and its own deny decisions, not by relying on a PermissionDenied event.
A synthetic Kookr toolkit plugin placed in the (isolated) ~/.grok/plugins/ user scope is discovered by `grok inspect --json` with provides.skills=1, hooks=true.
From an arbitrary cwd the model invoked the injected sentinel skill and emitted its unique token SKILL_SENTINEL_5E1D.
`grok inspect --json` lists both CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md under projectInstructions (fileType agents_md, scope project) in independent single-file cwds.

In two independent runs from non-Kookr cwds the model followed the project instruction file and returned the exact sentinels CLAUDE_SENTINEL_7F3A (CLAUDE.md-only cwd) and AGENTS_SENTINEL_9B2C (AGENTS.md-only cwd).

Under a real PTY the TUI reached readiness (honoring --no-alt-screen), accepted byte-level input, and the initial prompt/approval flow worked. Additionally confirmed through Kookr's own vendored dtach (vendor/dtach/dtach): grok launched detached, held a live socket, and accepted byte input via `dtach -p`, then drained cleanly on kill. Interactive user-driven deny signal shape is POC-B follow-up.

Success: Stop.reason=end_turn + clean exit(0) => completed. Failure (403): Stop.reason=error + StopFailure(http_status 403) + exit(1) => terminated; process evidence overrides. NOTE: SessionEnd does NOT fire in headless -p, so Kookr must classify from Stop.reason + process exit, not SessionEnd.

Satisfied via the correlation path: subagent_start carries a distinct subagentId (child) vs sessionId (parent) plus subagentType and a child transcriptPath. CONSTRAINT: enforceable disablement is NOT reliable — --no-subagents, --disallowed-tools spawn_subagent, and both combined all failed to prevent a spawn in headless -p (--disallowed-tools Task throws an internal error). Slice 1 must supervise subagents via correlation, not assume they are off. subagent_stop was not observed before headless process exit (late-event/drain concern).
SIGKILL of the owned PTY process tree drained every descendant (clean_drain=true). Default config spawns no detached leader daemon (no ~/.grok/leader.sock), so no orphaned backend survived.

constraints: Interactive injection: --plugin-dir is agent-only (interactive root `grok` rejects it). Toolkit distribution must sync into ~/.grok/plugins/ (mirroring the existing ~/.claude/plugins/ deploy flow); launch-scoped monitoring hooks must use per-session GROK_HOME composition, never a persistent ~/.grok mutation.

Hook schema divergence: Grok payloads are camelCase (sessionId, hookEventName, toolName, toolInput, subagentId) — a Grok-specific decoder is required; Kookr's snake_case parseHookEvent() cannot be reused unchanged.
Subagent disablement is not enforceable via tested flags; supervise children via subagent_start correlation instead of assuming they are disabled.
PermissionDenied event not observed for rule/hook denials in headless -p; detect blocks via PreToolUse-without-PostToolUse and Kookr's own deny decisions.
SessionEnd does not fire in headless -p; rely on Stop.reason + process exit for terminal classification.
Only this exact build (0.2.93 / f00f96316d / linux-x86_64 / glibc 2.35) is tested; other builds/platforms (incl. macOS) remain unqualified and may run only inside the POC runner.
Chat-endpoint access requires an account entitlement (console.x.ai); a plain grok.com OAuth login returns HTTP 403 at the chat proxy until enabled.
